transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — recording is on. quick intro, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Maya and Alex are here from engineering and CSM.
[00:00:12] Dr. Elena Cruz: Hi all, Elena here. we'll be short, want to make sure our compliance team is satisfied before we onboard.
[00:00:20] Tom Reynolds: Tom, SRE. main asks: KMS, RTO/RPO numbers, and how you handle failover.
[00:01:05] Maya Singh: Great. to kick off, SOC 2 reports we can share latest attestation — redacted. we also have ISO documents, but note some vendor names in the report might be slightly off due to automated redaction, apologies.
[00:01:45] Priya Kapoor: On the KMS front — we need a customer-managed key in our GCP project, HSM-backed if possible, and logs must stay in EU region. Is that supported?
[00:02:10] Maya Singh: Yes, BYOK supported. we have both cloud KMS integration and an HSM option for private deployments. logs can be configured to stay in-region — we map audit log storage to your retention policy. small caveat: for hosted inference there's a control plane that needs metadata, that stays in US for now but trace logs and PII-less audit artifacts can be sharded to EU.
[00:03:05] Marco Alvarez: That control plane thing — does that mean any metadata leaves the EU? we need to be careful with patient data residency.
[00:03:30] Jordan Park: short answer: no patient data moves. metadata is non‑PII routing info; but we can provide options for private control plane if needed.
[00:04:12] Tom Reynolds: Ok, good. walk me through RTO/RPO — realistic numbers for your Dedicated offering?
[00:04:35] Maya Singh: For dedicated pools with cold standby we target RTO ~15 minutes for endpoint failover, RPO depends on KV cache and replication. with continuous KV replication we can get sub-5 minute RPO for logs and checkpoint replication, for model state it's near-zero once warmed. note: for hoster burst cases, fallback to smaller model variants may increase latency but preserves availability.
[00:05:25] Dr. Elena Cruz: sub-5 minute RPO for logs is crucial — our compliance requires audit continuity. how are the audit logs signed and retained?
[00:05:47] Maya Singh: logs are append-only, signed with service KMS if you use Redwood-managed; with BYOK we sign with your KMS key. retention policies are configurable, we can push directly to your GCS/S3 in-region.
[00:06:30] Priya Kapoor: And access — who can see the logs? RBAC?
[00:06:45] Alex Chen: RBAC is role-based via our Console and we support SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO. you can map groups to roles (auditor, admin, developer). all API calls are logged and we can produce filtered export for auditors. there might be some naming inconsistencies in the auto-generated user metadata (SEVs in transcription, sorry) — we'll confirm mappings.
[00:07:30] Tom Reynolds: Escalation process — if production endpoint goes down at 2am, what's the path?
[00:07:45] Jordan Park: We have a 24/7 on-call for Dedicated customers with pager duty integration. first alert -> on-call engineer -> 15 minute TTR escalation -> on-call manager -> account team -> exec on-call for P1s. We'll share a matrix.
[00:08:50] Dr. Elena Cruz: We need at least two named escalation contacts in contract, with SLAs tied to response and restore windows.
[00:09:18] Jordan Park: Yes we can include named contacts and a blameless postmortem clause. SLA target we typically offer 99.95% for dedicated with credits and 15-minute initial response for P1.
[00:10:05] Priya Kapoor: For BCDR — do you run tabletop exercises with customers?
[00:10:22] Maya Singh: Yes, we offer runbook tabletop and can simulate region failover. last week we did a test with a healthcare customer — had a runbook that flipped over to a passive region and validated RTO.
[00:11:00] Tom Reynolds: Did that require data rehydration that impacted RPO?
[00:11:10] Maya Singh: It depends. if you use continuous replication and prefix caching, cutover is fast. big caveat is warm vs cold cache. if cache is cold, first requests will have higher latency and token counts; but we can pre-warm critical models as part of the playbook.
[00:12:05] Marco Alvarez: About pre-warming — who pays for warm standby capacity?
[00:12:20] Jordan Park: Typically shared cost model or reserved capacity line item in the Dedicated contract. we'll propose options in the pricing sheet.
[00:13:05] Priya Kapoor: Can we get a demonstration of the audit log export and signed receipts? that would help our auditors.
[00:13:18] Alex Chen: Sure — Maya can run a short demo next week, we'll prepare a scrubbing of real traffic. link to sample PDF and the drive will be shared.
[00:14:30] Dr. Elena Cruz: On the encryption front: key rotation policy? We have to rotate keys every 90 days.
[00:14:45] Maya Singh: BYOK supports rotation schedule and we support HSM rotation via your key management. automated rotation with grace windows is supported; we'll document the exact handshake on rotation so there's no decryptability gap.
[00:15:30] [00:15:30] (crosstalk) Marco Alvarez: having issues hearing, can you speak a little louder?
[00:16:00] Jordan Park: Sorry about that. quick note on audit exports — when we export logs to your bucket we include a signed hash manifest to verify integrity.
[00:16:42] Tom Reynolds: Good. are there any compliance gaps we should know about?
[00:16:55] Maya Singh: The main one is the hosted control plane's metadata residency for some hosted customers — many enterprise customers opt for Private control plane in EU to fully eliminate any US-hosted metadata. otherwise SOC2 and ISO artifacts are available.
[00:18:05] Priya Kapoor: Ok, show me the escalation timeline for P1 vs P2 in practice.
[00:18:20] Jordan Park: P1: initial response 15m, engineer TTR 60m aimed, escalation to manager 30m after no progress. P2: response 60m, TTR 4 hours targeted. All with follow-up postmortem within 72 hours. we'll put these in contract text.
[00:19:00] Dr. Elena Cruz: For our regulatory audit we'll need evidence of tabletop drills — can Redwood join our external audit?
[00:19:16] Alex Chen: yes we can provide artifacts and a Redwood witness. for on-site audit we can provide SOC2 bridge letter and demo of logging exports.
[00:20:10] Tom Reynolds: Can you summarize the fallback behavior if GPUs are saturated in a region?
[00:20:28] Maya Singh: Smart routing will fail over to another region or to a smaller quantized model variant. we keep isolated priority lanes for critical traffic and automatic model-variant fallback. this may increase latency but prevents total outage.
[00:21:45] Marco Alvarez: How do you ensure data is not leaked during failover?
[00:22:00] Maya Singh: Traffic is encrypted in transit and at rest. during failover we maintain encryption keys; with BYOK, keys are under your control so decryption can't happen without your key. we also scrub any ephemeral caches and rotate session keys post-cutover.
[00:23:15] Jordan Park: quick note — sample SLA and escalation matrix link: https://drive.google.com/sample-redwood-sla (will share real later).
[00:24:00] Priya Kapoor: Regarding retention: our policy requires 7 years retention for audit logs. is that supported?
[00:24:18] Maya Singh: yes, configurable, we'll export to your archival bucket with lifecycle rules. storage costs are passed through.
[00:25:30] Dr. Elena Cruz: One more question: can you support SAML 2.0 with IDP-initiated flows and SCIM for provisioning?
[00:25:45] Alex Chen: yes, SAML 2.0 supported, SCIM v2 provisioning supported. sometimes the auto-generated displayName field gets truncated by the IDP mapping — it's a known minor issue we've tracked.
[00:27:10] Tom Reynolds: Ok great. let's talk next steps and owners.
[00:27:25] Jordan Park: Recap: Jordan will send SLA draft; Maya will share KMS architecture and schedule onboarding workshop; Alex will prepare a sanitized audit log export demo; Priya will share retention, regulatory windows. we'll follow up with a calendar invite.
[00:28:02] Dr. Elena Cruz: thanks, appreciate it. any final concerns?
[00:28:20] Marco Alvarez: only that we get the runbook and a scheduled tabletop in writing.
[00:28:35] Maya Singh: will do.
[00:29:00] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone. recording stops.
